title: Sarva-Darsana-Samgraha
author: madhava
attributionNote: Attributed to Madhava Acharya, usually identified with the Advaita author and statesman Madhavacharya. The attribution is traditional rather than documentary.
description: A survey of the Indian philosophical schools in fifteen chapters, from the materialist Charvaka through the Buddhist and Jain systems to the six Brahmanical schools and finally Vedanta. Each system is presented through its own arguments before the author answers them from an Advaita position, which makes the work a history of philosophy and a polemic at once.
historicalContext: Written in fourteenth-century Vijayanagara. Cowell and Gough's 1882 translation was the first complete English rendering and remains the standard one; it arranges the chapters in the order of the printed Sanskrit editions.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1882 translation by E. B. Cowell and A. E. Gough is public domain in the United States.
